learning_outcomes.text: Students understand the structure and characteristics of science.
Students grasp the historical development of scientific studies.
Students grasp the impact of science on humans and society.
Students use topics related to the nature of science and the history of science in their lesson plans.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the concepts of culture, technology, science and philosophy.
Science in Mesopotamia
Science and Philosophy in Ancient Greece
Medieval Europe and Scholastic Philosophy.
Science and philosophy in the Islamic cultural geography: Ibn Khaldun.
Science and Philosophy in Renaissance Europe.
In the Age of Enlightenment and Positivism; Philosophy of Science
Vienna Circle
Karl R. Popper: The Logic of Scientific Discovery
Imre Lakatos: The Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes.
Karl R. Popper: Against Method.
Thomas S. Kuhn: The Structure of Scientific Revolutions.
Willard V. O. Quine: Two Dogmas of Empiricism.
Concepts related to science: Ontology, epistemology, science, scientific method
Philosophy of science: Popper and Kuhn
Philosophy of science: Lakatos and Feyerabend
Science in early civilizations
Science in the Ancient Greek world
Science and philosophy in the Islamic cultural geography: Ibn Khaldun
Medieval Europe and Scholastic Philosophy and Science
Science and Philosophy in Renaissance Europe
In the Age of Enlightenment and Positivism; Society and Philosophy of Science
Contributions of Turks to science in the Middle Ages
Galileo and his works
Einstein and his works
Science in the Republican period
Thomas Kuhn and Lakatos
assessment_rules: Midterm and final exam dates are not specified in the 14-week course schedule. Midterm and final exam dates are held on the dates specified in the academic calendar by the decision of the University Senate.
